method: I read the six reports, then re-opened the evidence and re-took every number I could. Clips were decoded with toolchain/ffmpeg/ffmpeg -fps_mode passthrough to one PNG per frame (256/314/395/300/304, confirmed against ffprobe nb_frames) and measured per frame with numpy/cv2; stills with PIL. Cross-cycle claims were checked with md5sum against evidence/.previous/ and with ffmpeg -f framemd5. I opened the sixteen evidence/scenes/*.json capture scripts, the five per-clip logs' fold and sensation blocks, logs/surfaces.json, logs/haptics.json, logs/scroll_webkit.json and logs/pwa.json, none or few of which any report cites. Every figure below is reproducible from evidence/ with python3 (PIL 12.3.0, numpy 2.4.6, cv2 5.0.0) and toolchain/ffmpeg.

gaps.what: The report's central cross-cycle measurement is false, and it is the one field DIFF.json assigns to this critic. coherence states 'Fourteen artifacts are byte-identical to evidence/.previous/' and fills all seventeen entries of its judgements block with 'unchanged - ssim 1.0, byte for byte the previous file'. No artifact is byte-identical. It also reports 08_state_propagating.mp4 as '5,380,163 bytes in both directories' with 'every one of its 395 decoded frames' sharing a framemd5 with the previous capture, 'confirmed pixel-for-pixel on ten full-resolution frames' - a measurement that cannot have been taken, since the previous file is a different length. Its cited SSIMs (1.0, 0.9931) appear nowhere in DIFF.json.
gaps.measurement: md5sum: all 14 artifacts present in both directories differ. Sizes differ for 13 of 14 (e.g. 06_unfolding.mp4 2,105,916 now against 2,616,470 before; 11_chat_scroll.mp4 9,544,537 against 6,162,308; 08_state_propagating.mp4 5,380,163 against 4,671,982 - not equal). ffmpeg -f framemd5: the current 08 has 395 frames, evidence/.previous/08_state_propagating.mp4 has 488, and 0 of the 395 hashes match any of the 488. Grayscale SSIM (11x11 gaussian, sigma 1.5) that I recomputed tracks DIFF.json rather than 1.0: 01_pulse 0.584 (DIFF 0.5262), 02_chat 0.533 (0.4794), 04_moments 0.450 (0.3844), 12_search 0.404 (0.3401), 17_setup_pwa 0.785 (0.7742); mean absolute difference against .previous runs 14.6 to 67.6 grey levels with 0.7M to 3.4M pixels differing by more than 10. DIFF.json's own range is ssim 0.3324-0.7742 against an unchanged threshold of 0.999.
gaps.where: evidence/critics/3/coherence.json judgements (all 17 entries), findings[6], and the closing sentence of the verdict; against evidence/DIFF.json and evidence/.previous/

gaps.kind: clip judged on the wrong reading; artifact nobody opened
gaps.what: material_truth's second blocking finding is that '06_unfolding.mp4 contains no unfolding' and that surfaces.json's 240-frame unfold_thirds sequence is 'absent from the capture'. The unfold is in the capture. It is the flat cream rectangle material_truth condemns in its first blocking finding: the sheet grows in thirds and ends with two crease bands. What is wrong is that 227 of the sequence's 240 rendered frames were never decoded, so the fold plays as an untextured field. The scene log that says so is cited by no report.
gaps.measurement: The lower sheet in 06 spans x50-769 on every frame. Its height goes 167 px at frame 16, 175 at 60, 268 at 100, 339 at 120, 383 at 180, 510 at 210, and holds at 510 through frame 255 - a 3.05x growth over 194 frames (3.1 s of app time). The final frame's sheet (y1232-1741) carries two dips in its row-mean profile at y1403-1409 and y1574-1580, about 8 grey levels deep and 7 px wide, cutting it into 173/171/165 px thirds. evidence/logs/06_unfolding.json reports fold {sequence: unfold_thirds, length: 240, decoded: 13, decoding: 0, playhead: 239, held_from: 227, held_to: 239} and a steps entry 'unfold' between the 16-frame and 240-frame runs. evidence/logs/surfaces.json reports fold_sequences.unfold_thirds {frames: 240, worst 2.125, median 3.003, below_floor 0, floor 1.2} - every asset frame carries paper. I reproduce material_truth's own numbers for the sheet: fill ratio 1.0000, top-edge std 0.00 px over 700 sampled columns, interior high-pass sigma-1.5 std 0.94 against 6.71 for the 'empty chair' note in the same frame, wood 1-4 px below it at 94.0 against 96.3 at 40-60 px. So one defect (a starved decode) was written up as two independent blocking findings, and its cause is misdiagnosed as an omitted asset.
gaps.where: evidence/critics/3/material_truth.json findings[0] and findings[1]; evidence/logs/06_unfolding.json reports[0].fold; evidence/06_unfolding.mp4 frames 16-255; evidence/crops/06_unfolding_strip.png

gaps.what: The third blocking finding - that the desk in 02_chat.png 'carries a tiled repeating scratch texture', with four hairlines at 67 px pitch at y1589-1601, four at 103-106 px at y2032-2036, four at 104-105 px at y2545, four at 64-65 px at y313-317 and four at 253-277 px at y437/y2568 - does not reproduce at any of the six named bands, and no autocorrelation supports tiling. This matters because 'a tiled repeating texture visible on a single screen' is a named below-floor condition and one of the three grounds the report gives for scoring 13.
gaps.measurement: y1589-1602, y2032-2037 and y2543-2548 are wood-only rows (all 1440 columns below grey 160). High-passing the row mean along x (gaussian sigma 15) and thresholding at 2 sigma returns zero runs of 8 px or more at any of the six bands. Scanning every wood-only row from y200 to y3100 for four or more evenly spaced bright runs at least 18 px wide (pitch std under 8 px) returns 0 rows out of the whole image. Horizontal autocorrelation of the widest all-wood band (y208-282, 74 rows x 1440 columns) peaks at 0.236 at lag 143 for lags of 20 or more; vertical autocorrelation over the left wood strip x0-46 full height has no local maximum at all above lag 20, only monotonic decay. A tile would give a peak near 1.0 at its pitch. anti_goal's independent autocorrelation on the 10_first_run desk agrees (their 0.136; my box gives 0.343 at lag 480). The report's separate serious finding that the desk is drawn rather than photographed does reproduce: high-pass sigma-1.5 std 5.07 at y1558-1605 against 11.63 for the note stock at the crops.json hand box, R/G channel-ratio std 0.017 against 0.089 on the note, wood 50.9 per cent of the frame.

gaps.what: The feeling picker's paper is translucent. The chat thread underneath it is legible through the sheet, so the ink of the notes below collides with the feeling labels on top. Three critics looked at this exact surface - emotional_transmission for the truncated family chips, coherence for the 'sixth visual language', material_truth for flat panels in 15 - and none reported that you can read through the paper. Paper is opaque; this is the same class of failure as a flat sheet, on the one surface where the six family names are ever shown to a reader.
gaps.measurement: 15_authored_feeling.mp4, region y370-520 x230-880 (the 'It was the good end' headline). With the picker closed at frame 0 the ink there reads at 146.4 grey levels of contrast against its surround. With the picker over it: 104.9 at frame 5, 62.9 at frame 10, 46.3 at frame 12, 21.3 at frame 15, 13.3 at frame 16 - so the picker never reaches opacity inside its own run - and the region still correlates r=0.598 with the picker-closed frame at frame 12. After the cut at frame 16 it returns: at frame 17, inside the sheet at y1500-1560 x180-900 (a band between two label rows that should be blank paper), 850 of 43,200 pixels sit below grey 150 with a minimum of 78, against 0 below grey 180 in the blank band at y460-560. The bleed-through is visibly the thread's own text - 'different thing and / you know it.', 'noor - travelling', 'empty chair', 'noor needs a lot' - printed across the picker.
gaps.where: evidence/15_authored_feeling.mp4 frames 0-30, the picker sheet at roughly y439-1908 x50-980

gaps.kind: clip measured on too few frames
gaps.what: All three critics found the millisecond readout over the composer, and all three understate how long it is on screen. Coherence also misreads the string: it quotes 'here - 2000ms - pass' where the pixels read 'here - 2000ms - page'.
gaps.measurement: Counting frames whose band y1990-2160 contains more than 50 pixels satisfying r>140, r-g>60, r-b>60 (the red playhead): 07_feeling_landing 314 of 314 frames, a single unbroken run 0-313 (100 per cent); 08_state_propagating 378 of 395, in runs 1-151 and 168-394, the gap coinciding with the run cut frames.json records at 167 (95.7 per cent); 15_authored_feeling 287 of 304, run 17-303 (94.4 per cent); 06_unfolding 0 and 11_chat_scroll 0. Against this, messenger says 'at least 2.48 s of app time (155 frames)', coherence says 370 of 395 for 08 from frame 25 and 280 of 304 for 15. The true figure for 08 is 6.05 s of its 6.32 s of app time. Reading the crop of frame 394 at 1:1 the string is 'here - 2000ms - page', matching logs/08_state_propagating.report.json sensation {feeling: here, channel: page, total_ms: 2000}.

gaps.what: The sixteen capture scripts in evidence/scenes/ are cited by no report. They settle messenger_reliability's blocking finding more strongly than it argues: the six absent messenger capabilities were never scripted to be captured, so their absence from the frames is not a rendering gap but a hole in the capture plan.
gaps.measurement: The complete verb vocabulary across all sixteen scenes is goTo (18), wait (28), shot (11), report (15), scrollTo (5), far (13), awaitArrival (10), frames (14), unfold (1), haptics (1), pair (1), step (1), timings (1), search (1), stage (1), openViewer (1), openCorner (1), sendFeeling (1), pwa (1). There is no verb for react, reply, edit, delete, attach, record a voice note or play a video. Every 'far' argument is one of: feeling {here, hold x2, nuzzle, soup x2, squeeze x2}, message x2, read, state mood restless, typing on. scenes/13_messenger_states.json - the scene whose whole purpose is messenger states - runs goTo, wait, scrollTo, wait, stage, wait, far read, wait, far typing on, wait, shot, report. The scripts also show all ten stills were taken at viewport 480x1040 dpr 3 (1440x3120) and all five clips at 360x780 dpr 3 (1080x2340), so every cross-artifact texture comparison in material_truth compares two different layouts at two different densities; no report says so.
gaps.where: evidence/scenes/*.json (16 files, 0 citations across the six reports)

gaps.kind: two reports contradict each other and neither is checkable
gaps.what: anti_goal's what_is_working asserts 'reactions render as plain grey Blu-Tack discs (13_messenger_states.png, y1780-1960 x220-700)'. messenger_reliability's blocking finding asserts 'no frame anywhere shows a reaction on a message'. The discs exist; nothing in the evidence says what they are, so anti_goal credits a capability it cannot identify and messenger denies a mark that is on screen.
gaps.measurement: 13_messenger_states.png carries two plain grey filled circles, roughly 55 px across, one at the left of the 'empty chair' caption and one at the left edge of the 'and the bread, if there is any' note near y1845 x290. They carry no glyph, no count and no label. logs/13_messenger_states.report.json's view block has fields for composer, attaching, replying_to, editing and partner_typing and no field for reactions; its visible list holds seven event ids and no reaction; scenes/13_messenger_states.json scripts no react step. evidence/reliability.json says react ok with detail 'reaction folded onto the target on the host, not a row' - consistent with a mark on a note, but the log is a separate 174-event scripted run, not this frame. The same frame also shows 'it would not go x' drawn in red, the only coloured ink in the picture.

gaps.kind: finding measured on too little of the evidence
gaps.what: The delivery-latency finding uses only 08's four arrivals. There are nine arrivals with a recorded waited_ms across the three paired clips, and the spread is wider than reported.
gaps.measurement: logs/08_state_propagating.json arrivals: 1928, 5601, 2596, 2007 ms. logs/07_feeling_landing.json arrivals: 4059, 1074, 2428 ms. logs/15_authored_feeling.json arrivals: 2701, 4966 ms. Nine arrivals, six over 1.9 s, two over 4.9 s, maximum 5601 ms for a plain text message - all over loopback, with reliability.json recording latency_ms 0 and no injected fault. Messenger's cold-start figures reproduce exactly, on the other hand: the six fresh seeded loads are 12019 (01_pulse), 11024 (06), 11612 (08), 11374 (14), 10988 (15), 11597 (dusk_pulse), against 2773-3180 ms for the seven 'kept' loads, and the two 1968/1988 ms loads are the unseeded first-run and setup scenes.

gaps.kind: claim resting on a method the evidence describes differently
gaps.what: The report credits sound as 'a third channel carrying the same envelope, not decoration'. The sound logs say the audio was muxed in afterwards by the capture harness from the asset file, not recorded from the running app, and the clip whose job is to show a feeling propagating carries no audio at all.
gaps.measurement: ffprobe: 07_feeling_landing.mp4 and 15_authored_feeling.mp4 each carry one h264 and one aac stream; 06_unfolding.mp4, 08_state_propagating.mp4 and 11_chat_scroll.mp4 carry a video stream only. logs/07_feeling_landing.sound.json states the method verbatim: 'aac 128k, the feeling's own ogg placed at its arrival, video stream copied'. The placement is accurate - decoding 07's audio at 8 kHz mono and taking per-frame RMS gives onsets above -60 dB at frames 1, 150 and 257 against sound.json's declared 0, 150 and 221, and frames 248-256 sit below -100 dB, reproducing the report's nuzzle off200 gap - but that measures the muxer, not the app. Three feelings land in 08 (hold, squeeze, here) with no sound on any of them.

gaps.what: The goal names 'an Apple-compatible installable PWA' as half the product. Coherence blocked on the missing Android artifacts and anti_goal read the PWA manifest name, but nobody examined logs/pwa.json or logs/17_setup_pwa.report.json for installability, and nobody read what 17_setup_pwa.png actually asks the iPhone owner to do.
gaps.measurement: logs/pwa.json is 342 bytes and is the whole of the evidence: manifest {name 'the other phone', display 'standalone', start_url '.', icons 4}, apple_touch_icon 'icons/Icon-192.png' (a 192 px Android/maskable size, not the 180 px face iOS takes for a home-screen icon), service_workers ['http://127.0.0.1:8798/push/sw.js'], display_mode_standalone false, browser webkit. No icon file, no meta tag inventory and no installed-state artifact exists anywhere in evidence/. 17_setup_pwa.png's own instructions require four manual steps of which one is 'install the profile the other phone is serving - open its address in Safari, take the profile, then trust it in settings under about, certificate trust settings', i.e. a hand-installed and hand-trusted CA on iOS. Nothing in the evidence shows that step, an installed icon, or the app running from the home screen. logs/17_setup_pwa.report.json records events 0, link 'connecting', setup_showing true - the only capture of the Apple path, taken against an empty store.

gaps.kind: gap in the material inventory both material critics leaned on
gaps.what: Both reports use logs/surfaces.json as the inventory that proves the objects and paper are textured. It covers 28 of the 36 feeling objects. Eight objects named by feelings have no surface entry, so their texture is unmeasured - including two that emotional_transmission and anti_goal cite by name as working.
gaps.measurement: logs/haptics.json names 36 distinct objects across 36 feelings (no object is shared). logs/surfaces.json's objects family holds 31 entries (patch_std 5.161-44.495, floor 2.0). Named by a feeling but absent from surfaces.json: obj_chair, obj_scribble, obj_spitball, obj_staple_chain, obj_string_loop, obj_thumbprint, obj_user_pigeon, obj_window - among them the thumbprint spiral for 'forehead' that emotional_transmission lists as working and the authored pigeon. Present in surfaces.json but bound to no feeling: obj_crown.webp, obj_gold_star.webp (patch_std 28.591) and obj_heart_fold.webp - anti_goal found the gold star and missed obj_crown, which is the same kind of token.
gaps.where: evidence/logs/surfaces.json surfaces (objects family, 31 of 327 entries); evidence/logs/haptics.json feelings[].object

gaps.what: code.json is the one report this pass cannot audit, since its nine rule verdicts rest on files outside evidence/. Of the three claims in it that can be checked against evidence/, two do not reproduce, and one of them contradicts itself inside the same paragraph.
gaps.measurement: Asset counts: code says '662 files under assets/. 660 have an entry', then quotes its own checker as reporting '658 files in assets/, 0 without an entry naming their generator'; evidence/logs/manifest.json says files 658, entries 790, without_an_entry [], entries_without_a_file 20, ok true. 662, 660, 658 and 790 are four different numbers for two quantities. Phantom entry: code names one manifest key outside the repository, '/tmp/.../scratchpad/fold_test/unfold_thirds/0090.png'; that path is not among the 20 entries in logs/manifest.json entries_without_a_file (which are one fonts index, one dusk paper webp, fifteen scratch/posters jpgs and five seed/photos jpgs). Coldstart timestamp: code says evidence/coldstart.json 'carries later_check.status pending checked_at 2026-09-06T09:23:26Z'; the file says 2026-09-06T09:26:17.951201Z. The one claim that does check out is the font bundle - logs/fonts.json lists exactly NoorHand.ttf and TeoHand.ttf and no DeskStamp face, and material_truth's reading of that file (floor_units 26.0 against min 18.8 and 11.7, too_close [], ok true) reproduces exactly.
gaps.where: evidence/critics/3/code.json rules[7], rules[8], findings[6]; against evidence/logs/manifest.json, evidence/coldstart.json, evidence/logs/fonts.json

gaps.what: Every clip plays 4.2 per cent slower than the app time it records, and no report says so, although several read durations straight off frame counts.
gaps.measurement: frames.json gives playback_over_app_time 1.042 for all five clips: each frame is one 16 ms step of the driven clock (62.5 steps per second of app time) assembled at 60 fps. So 06 is 4.10 s of app time played as 4.27 s, 08 is 6.32 s played as 6.58 s. Any duration read from a wall-clock position in a clip is 4.2 per cent long unless converted. frames.json also reports repeated_frames 0 and longest_still_run 0 for all five, which I confirm for 06: no adjacent pair is exactly equal and no adjacent pair falls below a mean absolute difference of 0.01, the quietest stretch (frames 210-255) still moving 0.03-0.09 grey levels per frame.

gaps.what: The search affordance collides with the thread's own dividers. In 11_chat_scroll the magnifier glyph and the word 'search' are drawn over a signal divider's timestamp, so the two overprint each other - the same class of composite coherence flagged for the day divider inside a note, on a different pair of elements.
gaps.measurement: 11_chat_scroll.mp4 frame 95, band y240-520: 'you is heads down' at left with 'Fri 24 Apr - 18:25' at right, and the search magnifier drawn on the '8' of 18:25 with the word 'search' extending past it to the frame edge. The same overlap recurs on 12_search.png where the type-filter row runs off the right edge: EVERYTHING, WRITTEN, PHOTOGRAPHS and VIDEO are whole and TALKING is cut through its final G at x=1440, with no scroll indicator - which reproduces messenger_reliability's minor finding exactly. coherence's grammar finding also reproduces exactly: 'you is heads down' and "you's phone is on normal" sit above a correctly formed "noor's phone is on normal" at frame 95.

gaps.what: Five of the ten derived crops and thirty of the fifty-four logs are cited by no report. The five clip strips are the cheapest possible read of each clip's arc, and the 06 strip alone shows the growing creased sheet that material_truth reported as an absent fold.
gaps.measurement: Cited by zero of the six reports: crops/06_unfolding_strip.png, crops/07_feeling_landing_strip.png, crops/08_state_propagating_strip.png, crops/11_chat_scroll_strip.png, crops/15_authored_feeling_strip.png, crops/02_chat_300_shadow.png, all sixteen evidence/scenes/*.json, and thirty logs including logs/06_unfolding.json (which holds the fold block), logs/13_messenger_states.report.json, logs/04_moments.report.json, logs/12_search.report.json, logs/14_media_viewer.report.json, logs/17_setup_pwa.report.json, logs/dusk_pulse.json and logs/recipes.json. The six panels of crops/06_unfolding_strip.png show the flat sheet appearing, growing and acquiring two crease lines across frames 0, 51, 102, 153, 204 and 255.

gaps.what: The blocking finding says video has 'no pictorial evidence at all' beyond search chips and reliability.json booleans. 04_moments.png carries six duration-badged tiles, which is on-screen evidence that video items exist in the log even though none is shown playing.
gaps.measurement: 04_moments.png shows a masonry of media tiles interleaved with torn paper labels reading 21s, 38s, 41s, 41s, 47s and 63s - durations, since 63 exceeds a minute hand. logs/04_moments.report.json confirms lens media 183, tiles_built 26, blobs {asked 18, arrived 18, reading 0, waiting 0}, so eight tiles have nothing in flight to fill them - and the bottom row of the frame is three blank cream tiles, mean 226.1 std 7.2 over y2760-2940 x24-470, which reproduces coherence's finding exactly. The images that do load are abstract renders (a sphere on a plane, a lit table, a grey sky band), reproducing anti_goal's point that no photograph of the couple appears anywhere.

coherence.why: The blocking finding stands and reproduces - MANIFEST.json records browser webkit for all fifteen artifacts, frames.json says scroll_emulator {missing: no Android device was up in this session}, and 09_two_devices.png and 16_setup_android.png are absent - and so do its 17_setup_pwa ground measurement (RGB 76.1/62.1/50.1 std 1.8 at x0-120 y300-900), its 'you is heads down' divider fault at 11_chat_scroll frame 95, its 04_moments blank tiles and its readout finding. But the one field DIFF.json hands to this critic by name - judgement - is wrong in all seventeen entries, and the measurement behind them ('byte for byte the previous file', 'all 395 decoded frames share the same framemd5') is contradicted by md5sum on every artifact and by a previous 08 that has 488 frames, not 395. A report whose closing sentence is 'by measurement, the same report the last capture would have earned' when nothing it measured is true should not score above a report that made no cross-cycle claim at all.

material_truth.why: The category is still below its floor of 22 and still blocked, but on one ground rather than three. The flat sheet in 06 reproduces to the digit (fill ratio 1.0000, top-edge std 0.00 px, interior high-pass 0.94 against 6.71 for the note beside it, contact shadow 94.0 against 96.3), as do the handwriting findings, the 'goodnight' shadow quad (564 pixels below grey 55, 160 above and 404 below the centroid, 307 left and 257 right, a 122-level step at x=1380) and the drawn desk (high-pass 5.07 against 11.63, R/G ratio std 0.017). But the second blocking finding is a misreading - the unfold is present and is the flat sheet, growing 167 px to 510 px with crease bands at thirds, starved to 13 decoded frames of 240 by the app's own log - and the third does not reproduce at all: no wood row in 02_chat.png carries four evenly spaced hairlines, and the strongest autocorrelation peak on the desk is 0.236, not a tile. Two of the three stated blocking grounds collapse into one defect and one non-finding.

code.why: Not because a rule verdict is wrong - this pass cannot see the tree and does not try - but because the report's meets_floor rests entirely on material no evidence-side critic can audit, and the three claims in it that touch evidence/ are two-thirds unreliable: four different numbers for the asset count in one paragraph (662, 660, its own checker's 658, and logs/manifest.json's 658 files / 790 entries), a phantom manifest key that is not among the twenty entries_without_a_file the evidence log actually lists, and a coldstart later_check timestamp three minutes off the one in the file. Its own notes admit it read docs/EVENT_TYPES.md against instruction. A score half a point above the floor should not rest on arithmetic that misses on the only lines a reader can check.
